511afdd00a12b45e07fcf51e49ea@global-arts.venue: Granoff Center for the Creative Arts
511afdd00a12b45e07fcf51e49ea@global-arts.address: Granoff Center for the Creative Arts
511afdd00a12b45e07fcf51e49ea@global-arts.description: In her practice, Dayanita Singh experiments with form through photography, architecture, and books to create exhibitions. Using these mediums, Singh extends an invitation to audiences to question how books, and book-making, might transform a space into an exhibition. This show takes cues from Singh’s artist-led approach to exhibitions to explore the relationship between “making” and “reading.” With Singh’s Book Building (2022) as a blueprint, this exhibition analyzes book-making as an artistic practice, material form, and conceptual process. Works in the exhibition span Singh’s career, including Book Building (2022), Blue Book (2009), File Room (2013), Museum of Chance (2014), and Sent a Let

23a173b4afc8092b962e6ae3d912@global-arts.description: Could the African American political tradition save American democracy? African Americans have had every reason to reject America’s democratic experiment. Yet African American activists, intellectuals, and artists who have sought to transform the United States into a racially just society have put forward some of the most original and powerful ideas about how to make America live up to its democratic ideals. bcd0b48dfb63603938e43854f3ac@global-arts.title: Food, Flow, Photography Gallery Presentation
bcd0b48dfb63603938e43854f3ac@global-arts.description: All are invited to a photographic poster presentation where students in the Food, Flow, Photography course will showcase their final projects! This unique class, supported by the Global Food Institute , Mechanical & Aerospace Engineering , and Corcoran School of the Arts & Design , brings science and art together. Students reveal the hidden physics of fluid flows (gases and liquids) through the art of cooking. They experimented with techniques to visualize flows in soups, sauces, mocktails, coffee, tea, caramelization, and more. It is science you can see and art you can feel. Mark your calendar and prepare to be amazed!

ff142e4ff5f89ad79a92934efa81@global-arts.title: Are You For Sale? LIVE! with Miguel Gutierrez and Jane Raleigh
ff142e4ff5f89ad79a92934efa81@global-arts.description: Join us for a live taping of Season 2, episode 2 of multi-disciplinary choreographer Miguel Gutierrez's podcast Are You For Sale? which examines the ethical entanglement between funding and dance-making. In this free public conversation, Miguel will talk to Jane Raleigh, former Director of Dance Programming at the Kennedy Center, about the current administration’s political assault on cultural spaces. Together they will discuss strategies for resistance and collectively ask, how do we continue to co-create nourishing art spaces? In the spirit of Are You For Sale? the conversation will be candid, cathartic, and community driven, so bring your questions for this live recording.

c4f14b8cb8c6d6f7ef269852c853@global-arts.title: National Symphony Orchestra: Handel's Messiah
c4f14b8cb8c6d6f7ef269852c853@global-arts.description: Hallelujah! You know the chorus, but there is a universe to discover beyond those famous four minutes. This December, early-music master Richard Egarr makes his NSO debut conducting Handels Messiah, the iconic holiday favorite that can be hushed, roaring, and wondrously divine. However you know Messiah as a yearly tradition, a piece you sang yourself, or music you have never heard live, there is nothing like being in the room when the first notes begin. There is a ticket limit of 8 tickets per person and per credit card on this event.

bbc5629581be71691f09b2f9dbe0@global-arts.title: Exhibit | Centering Philippine and Filipinx American Histories: Selections from The Bancroft Library
bbc5629581be71691f09b2f9dbe0@global-arts.description: The Bancroft Library’s collections of materials relating to the Philippines span nearly 500 years. Highlights in this exhibit include a transcript of an Inquisitorial trial from 1646, a prayer book written in the Cebuano language, and UC Berkeley Filipino student publications from 1905 to the present. The exhibit also features selections from the personal papers of acclaimed author Jessica Hagedorn, including typewritten drafts of her novels, poetry, song lyrics, and a screenplay, as well as childhood drawings and writings. Open hours may vary. Please view the The Bancroft Library hours page for the most up-to-date information.

e9114d3730acdfa9b16777cf7fc4@global-arts.title: Exhibit | Divestment Now! Student Activism and the Anti-Apartheid Movement at UC Berkeley
e9114d3730acdfa9b16777cf7fc4@global-arts.venue: The Rowell Exhibition Cases, Doe Library, 2nd floor
e9114d3730acdfa9b16777cf7fc4@global-arts.address: The Rowell Exhibition Cases, Doe Library, 2nd floor
e9114d3730acdfa9b16777cf7fc4@global-arts.description: In 1985, UC Berkeley students, with support from faculty, staff, and labor unions, transformed the campus into the heart of a powerful anti-apartheid divestment campaign. They organized rallies, teach-ins, and shantytown encampments to protest the university’s financial ties to companies profiting from South Africa’s system of racial segregation.

c1b1759e9291ea50cd46ac9e115d@global-arts.title: Exhibit | Kōmij Mour Ijin / Our Life Is Here
c1b1759e9291ea50cd46ac9e115d@global-arts.venue: Bernice Layne Brown Gallery (inside Doe Library)
c1b1759e9291ea50cd46ac9e115d@global-arts.address: Bernice Layne Brown Gallery (inside Doe Library)
c1b1759e9291ea50cd46ac9e115d@global-arts.description: Kōmij Mour Ijin / Our Life Is Here at Doe Library brings together reproductions of works and interpretive material from the 2023 voyage, exploring climate change, the legacy of US nuclear testing, and Marshallese knowledge and resilience.

73f2c2fedd0b93df7fb831b49638@global-arts.title: Photography Installation: Remembering the Future: Nuclear Testing, Rising Seas, and The Marshall Islands
73f2c2fedd0b93df7fb831b49638@global-arts.description: At Giannini Hall, 36 photographs selected from the recently published Remembering the Future: Nuclear Testing, Rising Seas, and The Marshall Islands (Radius Books, © 2026) by Mark Klett and William L. Fox extend the two men’s decades-long collaboration tracing the nuclear history of the American West and the broader Pacific sphere.

9183d501418b7b09e7da1d7ab7c6@global-arts.title: Thanksgiving Week Potato Party
9183d501418b7b09e7da1d7ab7c6@global-arts.description: Join us during Thanksgiving Week as we show our appreciation for the humble potato!

75a96d902ab5588e1429edd34881@global-arts.title: Film Screening: Modern Times
75a96d902ab5588e1429edd34881@global-arts.description: It starts with an overhead shot of sheep and cuts to the throngs coming out of a subway station. Was Charlie Chaplin a Surrealist, or just a realist? His version of modern times looks forward in equal measure to Jacques Tati and 1984 . This “silent” is full of modern sounds, heard over loudspeakers and big corporate television screens (not to mention the Tramp’s outburst of French-inspired gibberish). Charlie, the ever-elegant Tramp, is an industrial swashbuckler with an oilcan for a sword, but he’s begun taking on the characteristics of factory machines, obsessively twisting buttons no matter where they are.

9dfb90bf81c06f5cb576962d69ee@global-arts.title: Film Screening: The Last Waltz
9dfb90bf81c06f5cb576962d69ee@global-arts.description: Martin Scorsese grew up listening to seminal rock DJ Alan Freed, and from Mean Streets onward, his movies have been driven by the power of rock and roll. His love of music is innate and instinctual, so when The Band decided to hang it up after seventeen years on the road, they chose Scorsese to film their farewell concert at Winterland Ballroom on Thanksgiving 1976. The film intercuts the glorious music from one of the all-time great concert lineups with interviews with members of The Band as they talk about their lives and music. The Last Waltz is an elegiac masterpiece that captures a special moment in music history.

287ec890ea11268461ff5f4d935e@global-arts.title: Film Screening: Center Stage
287ec890ea11268461ff5f4d935e@global-arts.description: After a string of memorable performances as strong-willed, beautiful, and virtuous women, the actress Ruan Lingyu committed suicide in 1935, at the age of twenty-four. Stanley Kwan’s innovative film goes far beyond the traditional biopic to offer up several strata of “reality,” “reenactment,” and “cinema.” Detailed re-creations of scenes from the actress’s too-short life combine with documentary interviews of her contemporaries, actual footage from her existing silent films, and even discussions between star Maggie Cheung, Kwan, and other cast members. Like a Russian doll, Center Stage reveals a Modernist take on the ways in which cinema and culture create an actress, a legend, and a woman.

bcd993e5a8f84b13198c90777d4e@global-arts.title: Film Screening: Bellissima
bcd993e5a8f84b13198c90777d4e@global-arts.description: “What is acting after all?” Maddalena (Anna Magnani) rhetorically asks before the mirror in Luchino Visconti’s melodrama of mother love and misplaced ambition. Magnani’s extraordinary performance is its own answer. As a working-class mother desperate to get her young daughter a shot at stardom through a Cinecittà casting call, Magnani turns what might have been a simplistic caricature of a domineering stage mother into a fully rendered character, both hilarious and tragically human. Visconti’s direction similarly refuses to distinguish between satire and sincerity; even while it mocks the business of moviemaking, Bellissima is an exquisite example of the filmmaker’s craft.

b136666e8eaad45850922ebf268f@global-arts.title: Exhibit | Centering Philippine and Filipinx American Histories: Selections from The Bancroft Library
b136666e8eaad45850922ebf268f@global-arts.description: The Bancroft Library’s collections of materials relating to the Philippines span nearly 500 years. Highlights in this exhibit include a transcript of an Inquisitorial trial from 1646, a prayer book written in the Cebuano language, and UC Berkeley Filipino student publications from 1905 to the present. The exhibit also features selections from the personal papers of acclaimed author Jessica Hagedorn, including typewritten drafts of her novels, poetry, song lyrics, and a screenplay, as well as childhood drawings and writings. Open hours may vary. Please view the The Bancroft Library hours page for the most up-to-date information.

ba573abd3e2650a6fe9facee3f56@global-arts.title: The Dynamic! – Funny scenes, songs and games!
ba573abd3e2650a6fe9facee3f56@global-arts.description: The Dynamic! is an improv show that thrives on chaos, quick thinking, and whatever ideas the audience throws at the cast. Every scene, game, and musical moment is built in real time, and the performers lean into the unexpected with a mix of confidence, silliness, and genuine surprise. They know how to turn a wild suggestion or a joke that goes off the rails into something even funnier, and half the joy is watching them navigate the mess together. The show moves fast, the energy stays high, and no two nights ever feel the same. You help spark the fun, and the cast runs with it to create a comedy experience that feels alive, loose, and completely in the moment.

dd82f801dce1b52f21908652c457@global-arts.title: Business X Design: Alisa Barry of Bella Cucina and Smith Hanes of Smith Hanes Studio
dd82f801dce1b52f21908652c457@global-arts.description: Join MODA for the final session of our 2026 Business x Design season, facilitated by Gene Kansas. Alisa Barry grew Bella Cucina from a small Atlanta café into a line of artisan pantry goods sold around the world. Smith Hanes founded Smith Hanes Studio, the design firm behind some of Atlanta’s best-known dining rooms, including The Optimist and Atrium at Ponce City Market. Alisa and Smith will talk about how food, space, ritual, and atmosphere work together to create hospitality, and how each of them turned a personal craft into a values-driven business.

2b17dfe34c7480cb5a6e55ce6fa7@global-arts.title: Graphic Design Studio: Winter Travels
2b17dfe34c7480cb5a6e55ce6fa7@global-arts.description: Join MODA for a virtual studio and design a travel collection featuring an imaginary winter destination. In this virtual studio, young designers will explore how travel posters and postage stamps use illustration, typography, and bold compositions to inspire people to visit new places. Students will invent a magical winter destination such as a crystal forest, snowy kingdom, frozen waterfall, or floating ice island. Using Canva, they will create either a travel poster or a coordinated stamp collection that captures the atmosphere of their winter wonderland. At the end of the studio, students can share their work and receive feedback in a supportive environment.

fc0d9a7f6ee806fb56ff9af182fa@global-arts.title: The Dynamic! – Funny scenes, songs and games!
fc0d9a7f6ee806fb56ff9af182fa@global-arts.description: The Dynamic! is an improv show that thrives on chaos, quick thinking, and whatever ideas the audience throws at the cast. Every scene, game, and musical moment is built in real time, and the performers lean into the unexpected with a mix of confidence, silliness, and genuine surprise. They know how to turn a wild suggestion or a joke that goes off the rails into something even funnier, and half the joy is watching them navigate the mess together. The show moves fast, the energy stays high, and no two nights ever feel the same. You help spark the fun, and the cast runs with it to create a comedy experience that feels alive, loose, and completely in the moment.

8772e8e6b07a61e45049ffdb88eb@global-arts.venue: National Center for Civil and Human Rights
8772e8e6b07a61e45049ffdb88eb@global-arts.address: 100 Ivan Allen Jr. Boulevard NW, Atlanta, GA, 30313
8772e8e6b07a61e45049ffdb88eb@global-arts.description: Join us for UDHR Day at the National Center for Civil and Human Rights and enjoy free admission all day, generously supported by The Home Depot Foundation. UDHR Day commemorates the adoption of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, a landmark document affirming the rights and dignity of all people. Visitors of all ages are invited to explore the Center’s immersive exhibitions, engage with powerful stories of courage and change, and reflect on the ongoing pursuit of justice, freedom, and equality around the world.

ddc95e13a4bc1fd0927481993bf6@global-arts.title: A Winter in London
ddc95e13a4bc1fd0927481993bf6@global-arts.description: A WINTER IN LONDON | PLACE & BELONGING Where do we belong? A place is more than a point on a map. It is its people, traditions, memories, movement, sounds, and stories. In A Winter in London, our All Together Now journey turns toward place and belonging. Through the musical life of London, we explore how people give meaning to the places they inhabit, and how those places, in turn, become part of who they are. Together is where belonging begins: in the communities we inherit, the communities we enter, and the communities we help create. 693a7903bd103fe5b6fd63085f08@global-arts.title: The Dynamic! – Funny scenes, songs and games!
693a7903bd103fe5b6fd63085f08@global-arts.description: The Dynamic! is an improv show that thrives on chaos, quick thinking, and whatever ideas the audience throws at the cast. Every scene, game, and musical moment is built in real time, and the performers lean into the unexpected with a mix of confidence, silliness, and genuine surprise. They know how to turn a wild suggestion or a joke that goes off the rails into something even funnier, and half the joy is watching them navigate the mess together. The show moves fast, the energy stays high, and no two nights ever feel the same. You help spark the fun, and the cast runs with it to create a comedy experience that feels alive, loose, and completely in the moment.

8ee82ba274daba761f9cd9762ec0@global-arts.title: The Dynamic! – Funny scenes, songs and games!
8ee82ba274daba761f9cd9762ec0@global-arts.description: The Dynamic! is an improv show that thrives on chaos, quick thinking, and whatever ideas the audience throws at the cast. Every scene, game, and musical moment is built in real time, and the performers lean into the unexpected with a mix of confidence, silliness, and genuine surprise. They know how to turn a wild suggestion or a joke that goes off the rails into something even funnier, and half the joy is watching them navigate the mess together. The show moves fast, the energy stays high, and no two nights ever feel the same. You help spark the fun, and the cast runs with it to create a comedy experience that feels alive, loose, and completely in the moment.

Set to the timeless music of Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky, the production transforms the stage into a magical holiday experience. Now in its 34th year, the production continues to delight families across more than 80 cities annually.

Adapt. Stay available. Be efficient. Make the most of your time. Create. Monetize. Promote yourself. Discipline your body. Control your emotions. Outdo yourself. Do more. Do it faster. Don’t stop. UU.-Francia-Alemania, 2026, 18’)En el silencioso desierto del suroeste de Estados Unidos, un grupo de científicas simulan la colonización de Marte. Siguen protocolos, registran datos y viven sujetos a horarios precisos; y, sin embargo, en las pausas, lo ordinario se vuelve extraño. A Planet Painted by Hand se detiene en esos momentos para preguntarse cómo imaginamos la vida en un mundo que nunca hemos pisado.School Shooters: Tú me mataste primero (Miguel Ariza, España-Alemania, 2026, 22’)Tras graduarse, Jaime y Chloe preparan durante el verano una matanza en su instituto. f3cdbb026c39bc0339b5fdc58031@global-arts.title: Diario de una camarera
f3cdbb026c39bc0339b5fdc58031@global-arts.description: Radu Jude realiza una versión libre, mordaz y clarividente del clásico de Octave Mirbeau, también filmado por Jean Renoir y Luis Buñuel. Un retrato de los días previos a Navidad de una empleada doméstica rumana apasionada por el teatro al servicio de una pareja acomodada de Burdeos interpretada por Mélanie Thierry y Vincent Macaigne. Estrenada en Cannes, la última película del provocador cineasta rumano es una sátira social mordaz sobre las contradicciones de una Europa que se proclama igualitaria.

4901ee282958e9812c13dba27779@global-arts.title: Adiós, ríos
4901ee282958e9812c13dba27779@global-arts.description: Los habitantes de una aldea de montaña resisten a la despoblación y el aislamiento. Eladio, el guarda forestal de la comarca, va en busca de una osa que deambula por el valle. Cuando Xacobo, un anciano de la aldea, se pierde en el monte, los acontecimientos se suceden de forma inesperada mientras se traman historias de cuidado, pérdida y resistencia. Con fotografía de Ion de Sosa, el debut de Sebastián Uría reúne memoria y paisaje en una película de aliento poético donde la naturaleza sigue su curso, sin que la nostalgia lo ocupe todo.> Con la presencia del director.

6cd6a23b1156ad7374b6014a435f@global-arts.title: The Dreamed Adventure
6cd6a23b1156ad7374b6014a435f@global-arts.description: En Svilengrad, una pequeña ciudad de Bulgaria en la frontera con Turquía y Grecia, Veska, una arqueóloga, se cruza con Said, un viejo conocido al que le han robado el coche. A medida que se reencuentran, Veska se ve cada vez más inmersa en el turbio mundo del que Said ha salido, y pronto se embarca en su propia exploración sobre las redes criminales que se esconden bajo la superficie de esta ciudad aparentemente inocente en las afueras de Europa. Cuando figuras de su pasado comienzan a acecharla, Veska se ve obligada a enfrentarse a la verdad. Tras Western, la cineasta alemana Valeska Grisebach vuelve al género con un thriller fronterizo que combina ficción y documental.

a668392185c41e1389f0878e46bb@global-arts.title: Un arbre és un arbre
a668392185c41e1389f0878e46bb@global-arts.description: Old Tjikko: un árbol de 9.550 años que se yergue solitario en la tundra sueca. Surtsey: una isla nacida hace apenas 63 años frente a las costas de Islandia. Lotus gomerythus: el último y único ejemplar conocido de una especie vegetal descubierta en las Islas Canarias. A través de estos tres principales ejes de observación, y de muchas otras imágenes reunidas mediante un proceso que se prolongó durante más de diez años, el fotógrafo Aleix Plademunt y el cineasta Carlos Marqués-Marcet plantean una meditación sobre cómo construimos nuestro mundo a partir de la mirada y sobre la compleja relación entre las imágenes y la palabra hablada.> Con la presencia de los directores.

6908fb6200bde5890e02b2cff24e@global-arts.title: Le vertige + Unidentified Nonflying Objects (UNO)
6908fb6200bde5890e02b2cff24e@global-arts.description: Programa:Unidentified Nonflying Objects (UNO) (Unidentifizierte Unflugobjekte (UUO)) (Sasha Svirsky , Alemania, 2026, 12')Por duradero y estable que parezca, todo orden puede acabar desmoronándose cuando la realidad que queda fuera del sistema irrumpe en él y, como la materia orgánica, crece hasta atravesar los límites que ese orden impone.Le vertige (Quentin Dupieux, Francia, 2026, 67')Jacques va a casa de su amigo Bruno para darle una noticia importante: toda la humanidad vive en una simulación. El siempre provocador y delirante cineasta francés firma una comedia absurda y existencial en animación 3D sobre la filosofía barata y las teorías conspirativas.

1c375a4e6c31ceb7d49c5a785879@global-arts.title: Seize moments de ma vie + Ghazal-e Sorkh
1c375a4e6c31ceb7d49c5a785879@global-arts.description: Programa:Ghazal-e Sorkh (Maryam Tafakory, Irán-Reino Unido-Francia, 2026, 19')En 1976 se hizo un llamamiento a boicotear el Festival de Artes de Shiraz. Algunos artistas de renombre internacional se sumaron de inmediato. Otros lo hicieron a regañadientes. «Los gigantes no vienen este año», escribió el diario iraní Kayhan. Entre fragmentos de películas encargadas por el sah y las películas y los libros prohibidos en aquellos mismos años, se entretejen historias que nacen de poemas «generadores de delitos». Todas vuelven a un fuego que nunca dejó de arder.Seize moments de ma vie (Albert Serra, Francia-España, 2026, 86')En un gesto apoteósico, Ingrid Caven y los bañolinos Molforts se encuentran

d9521527ddbecf1642178c0f37df@global-arts.title: Heil Jupiter!
d9521527ddbecf1642178c0f37df@global-arts.description: Rodeados por las grandiosas rocas de una playa mexicana, dos parejas de jóvenes pintores se saltan las normas morales establecidas, mientras una extraña y oscura figura los observa. Su audacia será juzgada y castigada, sellando sus destinos para siempre. El cineasta mexicano vuelve a ensanchar los límites del cine en este ataque frontal al poder, la falsa moral y a la violencia.> No recomendada para menores de 18 años.

5c700d6ba0f6a59f593b4e9fe14d@global-arts.title: The End of It
5c700d6ba0f6a59f593b4e9fe14d@global-arts.description: La inmortalidad también cansa. En un futuro distópico donde la vida eterna ya es una realidad, Claire, una reconocida artista convertida en joyera de lujo, decide poner fin a una existencia consumida por el aburrimiento justo antes de cumplir 250 años. Decidida a convertir su despedida en una última reivindicación artística, su deseo choca con quienes no están preparados para dejarla marchar. Con Rebecca Hall, Gael García Bernal y Noomi Rapace al frente del reparto, esta ópera prima combina humor, terror y ciencia ficción para explorar la obsesión por la eterna juventud.

7fb27cc9ba1465aa27555c51ecc5@global-arts.title: OpenLAB 2026 | The Golf Between Us – Talk by Wassim Alsindi
7fb27cc9ba1465aa27555c51ecc5@global-arts.description: As a result of software’s evolution from drab infrastructure into all-pervasive regime, computation is well past the point of modelling reality; it now actively re-engineers physical space to accord with its desiderata. Alsindi calls this spatial and material externalisation of computational logic upon our built environments Golf Futurism. From desert megacities to post-industrial urban regeneration projects, complex ecosystems and civic spaces are being stripped of their interiority and heterogeneity and flattened into hyper-manicured, privatised enclaves. 49ca9ab391b12c35c1a387721b4b@global-arts.title: OpenLAB 2026 | Internet Archaeology: Tracing Truths in Digital Ruins – Talk by Sophie Publig
49ca9ab391b12c35c1a387721b4b@global-arts.description: What gets lost when a screenshot or meme reaches us without its history? Platforms disappear, links rot, contexts collapse. Yet memetic fragments keep circulating, accumulating and actualising new meanings wherever they resurface. Internet archaeology starts from these digital ruins and follows the red string backwards, tracking artefacts across platforms, archives and increasingly obscure rabbit holes to excavate their buried contexts and sedimented meanings. Drawing on research on memes, semiotics and Digital Occultism (with Mikkel Rørbo), Publig reads mutation and repetition as clues, without losing sight of the thin line between critical pattern recognition and conspiratorial overconnect

f4e4d2b6596ed0172ec76b713a72@global-arts.title: OpenLAB 2026 | Visual Trust. A Multi-modal and Experimental Project – Presentation by Amanda Bernal Pérez
f4e4d2b6596ed0172ec76b713a72@global-arts.description: What makes people from different cultures and societies trust (or distrust) an image? How is the visual fake assessed and debunked in science, religion, AI or documentary photography? What is the relation between image-making and visual trust? Amanda Bernal introduces Visual Trust, an experimental and multimodal research initiative funded by the European Research Council (2021-2027). Drawing mainly on anthropology, the project takes a comparative approach to current regimes of visual authenticity and forgery. 7077de4b33300afa026e7a9d62bb@global-arts.title: OpenLAB 2026 | Excavando las redes: en busca de verdades entre ruinas digitales - Conferencia de Sophie Publig
7077de4b33300afa026e7a9d62bb@global-arts.description: ¿Cuántas cosas se han perdido en el instante en que nos llega esa captura de pantalla, ese meme sin historia? A nuestro alrededor las plataformas desaparecen, los enlaces se pudren, los contextos colapsan. Aun así, los fragmentos meméticos siguen circulando, acumulándose y activando nuevos significados allí donde resurgen. La arqueología de internet parte de estas ruinas digitales y tira del hilo rojo hacia atrás: rastrea artefactos a través de plataformas, archivos, rabbit holes y rincones cada vez más recónditos de la red para desenterrar sus contextos y sus significados sedimentados. En su investigación sobre memes, semiótica y “ocultismo digital” (con Mikkel Rørbo) Sophie Publig lee muta

c2cc632fdb038afee1be7177b2fb@global-arts.title: OpenLAB 2026 | El golf(o) que nos separa – Conferencia de Wassim Alsindi
c2cc632fdb038afee1be7177b2fb@global-arts.description: Desde que el software pasó de ser una infraestructura anodina a convertirse en un régimen omnipresente, la computación ha dejado muy atrás la fase de modelar la realidad: ahora rediseña activamente el espacio físico para que responda a sus designios. Alsindi llama Golf Futurism a esta externalización espacial y material de la lógica computacional sobre nuestros entornos construidos. De las megaciudades en el desierto a los proyectos de regeneración urbana postindustrial, ecosistemas complejos y espacios cívicos se ven despojados de su interioridad y su heterogeneidad, y reducidos a enclaves privatizados y recortados al milímetro. 9d5d1e7706b1907bf32f2bfc1c1f@global-arts.title: OpenLAB 2026 | Horrores encriptados: los Lost Media en el folclore digital – Conferencia de Arianna Caserta
9d5d1e7706b1907bf32f2bfc1c1f@global-arts.description: En un mundo hipervisual donde casi nada escapa al panóptico digital, los lost media son artefactos paradójicos: fragmentos de cultura mediática cuya existencia es objeto de rumores y de los que solo permanecen rastros parciales. Se buscan colectivamente en Reddit y YouTube, a medio camino entre el folclore en línea y la resistencia a la transparencia absoluta de las grandes plataformas. Así, recuperan algo del «aura» de los objetos de culto: importa más que existan que llegar a verlos. Como las creepypastas, su incompletitud y su ambigüedad estimulan la creación colaborativa de mitos. Y acercan los lost media al terror. e894eaf73589d87204a62ab4d926@global-arts.description: Lost in the Slop relata los viajes de Franziska Von Guten, una internauta de profesión convertida en viajera errante. En lugar de empezar por la punta del iceberg de internet y descender hacia sus aguas oscuras y profundas, Franziska traza las nuevas y sinuosas geografías de las redes. Un mundo moldeado por comunidades de nicho y bosques oscuros, pero también por lurkers y usuarios anónimos en las secciones de comentarios, que quizá no tengan nada en común salvo una sugerencia en la página «Para ti», un lenguaje visual compartido o una vibe. 3962bc5b5a24900cccb62702c642@global-arts.description: Wikipedia 2030: ¿quién sostendrá el conocimiento libre? Grokipedia nació en octubre de 2025 con la promesa de Elon Musk de superar a Wikipedia. ccd3d62f4cb303ddf635f43238d2@global-arts.description: In her practice, Dayanita Singh experiments with form through photography, architecture, and books to create exhibitions. Using these mediums, Singh extends an invitation to audiences to question how books, and book-making, might transform a space into an exhibition. This show takes cues from Singh’s artist-led approach to exhibitions to explore the relationship between “making” and “reading.” With Singh’s Book Building (2022) as a blueprint, this exhibition analyzes book-making as an artistic practice, material form, and conceptual process. c3c14a0604fd1911666ee5544baa@global-arts.title: Exhibit | Centering Philippine and Filipinx American Histories: Selections from The Bancroft Library
c3c14a0604fd1911666ee5544baa@global-arts.description: The Bancroft Library’s collections of materials relating to the Philippines span nearly 500 years. Highlights in this exhibit include a transcript of an Inquisitorial trial from 1646, a prayer book written in the Cebuano language, and UC Berkeley Filipino student publications from 1905 to the present. The exhibit also features selections from the personal papers of acclaimed author Jessica Hagedorn, including typewritten drafts of her novels, poetry, song lyrics, and a screenplay, as well as childhood drawings and writings. Open hours may vary. Please view the The Bancroft Library hours page for the most up-to-date information.

baae5cfe36b38e4109d607a830db@global-arts.title: Film Screening: The Last Waltz
baae5cfe36b38e4109d607a830db@global-arts.description: Martin Scorsese grew up listening to seminal rock DJ Alan Freed, and from Mean Streets onward, his movies have been driven by the power of rock and roll. His love of music is innate and instinctual, so when The Band decided to hang it up after seventeen years on the road, they chose Scorsese to film their farewell concert at Winterland Ballroom on Thanksgiving 1976. The film intercuts the glorious music from one of the all-time great concert lineups with interviews with members of The Band as they talk about their lives and music. The Last Waltz is an elegiac masterpiece that captures a special moment in music history.

69850be012f059b844ffddf2d11b@global-arts.title: Film Screening: Center Stage
69850be012f059b844ffddf2d11b@global-arts.description: After a string of memorable performances as strong-willed, beautiful, and virtuous women, the actress Ruan Lingyu committed suicide in 1935, at the age of twenty-four. Stanley Kwan’s innovative film goes far beyond the traditional biopic to offer up several strata of “reality,” “reenactment,” and “cinema.” Detailed re-creations of scenes from the actress’s too-short life combine with documentary interviews of her contemporaries, actual footage from her existing silent films, and even discussions between star Maggie Cheung, Kwan, and other cast members. Like a Russian doll, Center Stage reveals a Modernist take on the ways in which cinema and culture create an actress, a legend, and a woman.

e09d162498ca89a67ef32f2d41da@global-arts.title: Film Screening: Modern Times
e09d162498ca89a67ef32f2d41da@global-arts.description: It starts with an overhead shot of sheep and cuts to the throngs coming out of a subway station. Was Charlie Chaplin a Surrealist, or just a realist? His version of modern times looks forward in equal measure to Jacques Tati and 1984 . This “silent” is full of modern sounds, heard over loudspeakers and big corporate television screens (not to mention the Tramp’s outburst of French-inspired gibberish). Charlie, the ever-elegant Tramp, is an industrial swashbuckler with an oilcan for a sword, but he’s begun taking on the characteristics of factory machines, obsessively twisting buttons no matter where they are.

1cd625a1584b90bb4daeb2bcff39@global-arts.title: OpenLAB 2026 | Visual Trust. A Multi-modal and Experimental Project – Presentation by Amanda Bernal Pérez
1cd625a1584b90bb4daeb2bcff39@global-arts.description: What makes people from different cultures and societies trust (or distrust) an image? How is the visual fake assessed and debunked in science, religion, AI or documentary photography? What is the relation between image-making and visual trust? Amanda Bernal introduces Visual Trust, an experimental and multimodal research initiative funded by the European Research Council (2021-2027). Drawing mainly on anthropology, the project takes a comparative approach to current regimes of visual authenticity and forgery. Drawing on Gottesman’s deep engagement with the novel, NIGHT AND DAY considers how artists create, communicate, and sustain cultural memory within and against conditions of censorship, political repression, and state violence.
